::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Why is this subset closed](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2025557/why-is-this-subset-closed), asked by [JDoe](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/351993/jdoe) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2016-11-22; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I try to understand the following statement:
>
> Let $L(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R}^m)$ denote the vector space of linear maps from $\mathbb{R}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}^m$. Now the statement is that the set
>
> $S := \{\phi \in L(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R}^{m-k})~|~ \text{rank}(\phi)<m-k \}$ is a closed subset in $L(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R}^{m-k})$.
>
> Can anyone tell me why that is? Thanks!
:::

Here is a hint.  Consider the special case $m=n$ and $k=0$.  Then $S$ consists of square matrices with rank less than $n$.  This is the same as the set of matrices with zero determinant.  Since the determinant is a continuous function on $L(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R}^n)$ (I assume this is true in your chosen topology), and $S$ is the inverse image of the point $0$, then $S$ is closed.

Now in general, you can still use the determinant, or many determinants, to determine rank.
